what_it_does: Training a very large AI language model (an LLM) normally requires renting or owning a cluster of hundreds or thousands of specialized AI servers connected by expensive proprietary networks (such as InfiniBand or NVIDIA's NVLink). This paper describes Vela, a system that runs that same large-scale training on ordinary cloud infrastructure: standard virtual machines connected by commodity Ethernet using a protocol called RoCE (Remote Direct Memory Access over Converged Ethernet, which lets computers transfer data to each other's memory without burdening their main processors). The key engineering challenge is that the usual virtualization layer (the software that splits one physical server into many virtual servers) tends to slow down the high-speed memory transfers that GPU training depends on; Vela solves this with a combination of hardware and software techniques that let GPUs in different virtual machines copy data directly to each other's memory. The authors ran this system at IBM Cloud on about 1,500 NVIDIA A100 GPUs to train a 50-billion-parameter model for two and a half years and share lessons from that production experience.
